title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 + fused rope/rotary + kv/continuous-batching + scheduler tweaks
author: Ravi Patel
release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 variant with fused rope/rotary support, KV-friendly fused ops, continuous batching improvements, and scheduling heuristics. Expect 15-35% throughput gains on long-context workloads and improved tail latency. No API change.
description:
Context: our current attention kernels show suboptimal throughput for long-context and KV-heavy workloads and cause tail-latency spikes under high-concurrency scheduling. This PR upgrades the attention implementation to a FlashAttention v2 derivative with several Redwood-specific changes: fused rope/rotary computations, fused KV ops for cache-friendly layouts, and integration with the continuous-batching engine and the request scheduler. Motivation: reduce per-token cost and improve stable latency for production reroutes and streaming chat workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Replace baseline attn kernels with FlashAttnV2-derived kernels and wrapper toggles to fall back when unsupported.
- Fuse rotary/rope computations into the attention kernel path to avoid extra memory passes.
- Add fused KV write/read paths that align with our KV cache layout (interleaved blocks) to reduce memory copies.
- Hook kernels into continuous batching path (enable 1) steady-state multi-request batching, 2) early-exit for short sequences to reduce latency).
- Scheduler heuristics: new decision point that routes long-context requests to the fused kernels and small/low-latency requests to the low-latency path.
- Add feature gates, runtime flags, and extensive unit/integration tests.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel integration + unit tests
- [x] Continuous batching integration & regression tests
- [x] Scheduler heuristic + canary config
- [x] End-to-end perf benchmarks (internal)
- [x] Docs + feature flagging notes

Notes on compatibility: The new kernels are enabled by default on CUDA 12+ GPUs with sm>=80; there is a runtime fallback for older GPUs. No public API surface changes.

Rollout plan: Canary run on dedicated pool redwood-dedicated-canary for two weeks, then progressive rollout across regions with automated rollback if perf regressions are detected (linked to ENG-3245).
